newsitem.title: UK: UK April bank mortgage lending rises 740 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK April bank mortgage lending rises 740 mln stg.

text.p: Net lending to house buyers by Britain's major banks rose a seasonally adjusted 740 million stg in April, similar to the March rise and the recent monthly average, the British Bankers' Association said.
Unadjusted gross loans rose to 2.366 billion stg in April from a revised March figure of 2.114 billion.
The number of new mortgage approvals rose to 46,512 in April from 39,642 in March while their value rose to 2.785 billion stg from 2.312 billion.
The average value of approvals rose nine percent to 59,900 stg.
BBA director-general Tim Sweeney said the consistent growth in mortgage business in recent months continued in April.
"Though comparisons with figures a year earlier are difficult, it is clear that month-on-month figures for both net and gross lending are now noticeably stronger than 12 months ago," he said.
"Prospects for future lending also appear good, with approvals being higher in April than in the peak month of October last year, and by some margin."
The BBS figures, together with those recently published by building societies, suggested a strengthening in the total mortgage market in April, although with regional variations, Sweeney said.
